item.title: Java Techniques for Executing External Shell Scripts and Commands
item.description:
“Java Techniques for Executing External Shell Scripts and Commands”

How can a Java application reliably execute external operating system shell scripts or commands, and what are the recommended approaches versus potential pitfalls? Executing external processes from Java involves interacting with the underlying OS, which requires careful handling of environment variables, working directories, and input/output streams. Several standard and third-party methods exist for this purpose.

Preferred Method: Utilizing ProcessBuilder for Advanced Control

The ProcessBuilder class offers a more flexible and robust mechanism compared to the older Runtime.exec() method, especially when dealing with arguments, environment configuration, and working directories.
